title: Thule (ancestral Inuit) spread to Greenland
place: Alaska across Arctic Canada to Greenland
summary: Thule people, ancestors of today's Inuit, moved east from Alaska from about 1000 CE and reached Greenland by the 13th century. Genetics shows they replaced the earlier Dorset Paleo-Inuit by about 1300 CE.
why: Today's Inuit descend from this second Arctic migration, not the first.
